result:
Round 91 passes with 0 bugs. Every acceptance row that can run here was checked in a real browser (`browserVerified` and `realVerified` are true). Only one sub-check is blocked, because it needs the backend.

| Row | Result |
|---|---|
| **Source unchanged** | PASS. Same base commit at start and end, 8 changed files and 2 new ones, all 506 frozen files unchanged, hashes match A's. A's edits touch only the lines the task allowed, and the protected files are untouched. |
| **WAV memory, 10-minute export** (main check, 1440) | PASS in 3 of 3 runs, each in a fresh browser with nothing else running. Peak memory rose 529 / 543 / 531 MB against a limit of 639 MB (before this change it was 739–748 MB). That is about 196–219 MB less, close to the one float copy (~234 MB) the change was meant to remove. Each file was the correct 24-bit/48 kHz/stereo WAV with 29 206 176 frames, no NaN, matching RMS and the exact done message. |
| **5-minute WAV** (1280 and 1440) | PASS. Correct file, exact done message, and the exact overload warning `…498 sample…`. That count shows the WAV worker still measures before it clamps, and the worker really ran in both viewports. |
| **Cancel while the WAV is being written** (1280) | PASS twice. Exact cancelled message, no download within 15 s, the worker closed 496 ms after the click, and the next export worked. |
| **WAV + MP3 note** (both viewports) | PASS. The text matches the new wording exactly. It sits on two lines, fully visible inside the dialog and not cut off, with the footer buttons still visible. The WAV + MP3 export produced both files and the exact done message. |
| **MP3 timeout text** (1440) | PASS. With the encoder download held open, the exact new alert appeared 121.2 s after the Export click (120.0 s after the loading label), with no download. Retrying in the same page, without a reload, produced a 304.406 s MP3 and the exact done message. That makes the new "try again" wording true. |
| **Memory kept after cancel** (evidence only, never a fail this round) | Not reproduced at this resolution. About 26–29 MB was retained per pair, below the 58 MB threshold. Caveat: every cancel landed at 4%, and I did not confirm whether the render buffer is already allocated that early. |
| **Network and console** | PASS. No encoder download before the first MP3 click, then only the two ffmpeg core files. No studio-token, R2 or download requests and no `Authorization` headers. No real console errors or hydration warnings. |
| **Purchase protection** | PASS. Anonymous `/studio/middle-east` asks for sign-in and shows no workspace, the anonymous token request returns 401, and the header link opens `/studio-lab` with the demo badge. |
| **A's targeted tests** | PASS: 66 files, 1134 tests. |

**Blocked:** the fake-Bearer 403 check returned 500 because the backend is unavailable in the cloud. It is listed as blocked, not passed, and still needs a backend-enabled check.

**Not reachable in the browser:** the no-Worker fallback (unchanged) and the worker editing its arrays in place, which only the unit tests cover. The browser evidence for the in-place change is the memory drop plus the 498-sample warning.

**Environment, not app bugs:**
- My first visit to `/` made Vite re-optimize and reload every open page, which killed one parallel batch. I re-ran those rows on their own and they were clean; the failed logs are in `c-round-91/out/env-invalid/`.
- The 5-minute WAV files differ by tiny amounts between sessions (RMS agrees to about 1e-13). This rendering drift already existed before this round; it is noted for B as data only.

**For B:** the last SRW-20 stage is verified, so SRW-20 can close once the gate passes, and the architecture checkpoint q14 comes next. If you want more certainty on the cancel-memory question, a test that cancels later in the render, or on the 10-minute project, would settle it.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `c-round-91.md`
- `c-round-91.json`
- `c-round-91/` (tools, raw output, screenshots, test log, start/end hashes)
